core_conclusion: Current public evidence is already useful for turnout and directional political context, but this pass did not identify a methodologically credible representative party vote-intention poll that can directly supply national party vote shares. No arbitrary national percentages are therefore emitted.

signals.observed: The House of Representatives election is scheduled for 23 September 2026.

signals.method: CATI; n=1006 randomly interviewed; sample redressed to HCP RGPH 2024 population structure; stated maximum margin of error +/-3%

signals.warning: Non-random partial local elections cannot be converted directly into national legislative vote shares.

signals.observed: Reporting describes an open contest among RNI, PAM and Istiqlal, with PAM showing visible recent momentum, RNI retaining a powerful machine, and Istiqlal remaining a serious contender.
Fouzi Lekjaa was reported as officially joining the PAM leadership on 25 July 2026; Yanja El Khattat also joined after leaving Istiqlal.
A low-volume winner market exists for the 2026 Moroccan legislative election.
signals.warning: Winner probabilities are seat-rank beliefs, not national vote intentions, and market depth is limited.

explicit_exclusions.reason: No representative sampling frame; cannot be interpreted as national voting intention.
Seat outputs are downstream consequences and cannot be inverted into an independent national-vote input without circularity.
Narrative direction can define features but cannot justify hand-entered percentage-point adjustments.

next_data_objective: Find or construct a reproducible national party-strength estimate using representative vote-intention evidence if available, otherwise a historically validated model combining 2021 national base rates with comparable revealed electoral/candidate/turnout covariates.
